claim: Epoch AI finds frontier open-weight models lag the most capable closed models by an average of about 3.5 months (~7 ECI points) on the Epoch Capabilities Index.
quote: frontier open-weight models lag behind the most capable models by an average of 3 months ... Time gap: 3.5 months (with 90% confidence interval of 1.1 to 5.3 months) ... Performance gap: Approximately 7 ECI points

claim: By May 2026 Epoch's updated analysis put the open-to-closed lag at about four months (an 8-point ECI gap), slightly wider than the ~3 months measured through October 2025.
quote: Open-weight models lag frontier closed models by 'an average of four months' ... This represents an 8-point gap on the Epoch Capabilities Index ... The expansion from a three-month to four-month lag suggests the performance differential ... is gradually increasing.

claim: On SWE-bench Verified, closed Claude Opus 4.7 scores 87.6% versus open Nemotron 3 Super 120B at 60.47%, but the reasoning-benchmark gap has fallen from 30+ points in 2024 to roughly 3-8 points in 2026.
quote: Claude Opus 4.7 (closed): 87.6% ... Nemotron 3 Super 120B (open): 60.47% ... The gap is not the 30+ points it was in 2024; in most categories it now sits in the 3 to 8 percentage point range

claim: Artificial Analysis tracks an Openness Index and Intelligence Index measuring how close open-weight models are to frontier proprietary systems.
quote: Introducing the Artificial Analysis Openness Index

claim: On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (April 18, 2026) the best open-weight model GLM-5.1 scores 51 versus frontier models Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.4 tied at 57, a 6-point gap.
quote: GLM-5.1: Score of 51 ... The frontier closed models at the top score 57 (Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, GPT-5.4 xhigh) ... a 6-point gap between the highest-ranked open-weight model (51) and the tied frontier models (57) as of April 18, 2026

claim: On LMArena/Chatbot Arena in 2026 the top proprietary model GPT-5.5-high scores 1506 Elo while the best open-weight models GLM-5.1 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro tie at 1467, a 39-point gap.
quote: GPT-5.5-high leads with an Arena Elo of 1506 ... GLM-5.1 (MIT license): 1467 Elo ... DeepSeek-V4-Pro (MIT license): 1467 Elo ... The difference ... is 39 points (1506 - 1467)

claim: On SWE-bench the spread between the top model and the 10th-ranked model fell from 11.9% to 5.4% in a single year, reflecting rapid bunching of frontier and near-frontier (including open) models.
quote: The gap between top and 10th-ranked models fell from 11.9% to just 5.4% in one year.

claim: On LiveCodeBench, a contamination-free competitive-programming benchmark, both GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.5 score above 85%, with open-weight GLM-4.7 Thinking the leading open coding model in 2026.
quote: Both GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.5 score above 85% on LiveCodeBench. GLM-4.7 Thinking is the top open-weight coding model in 2026, while DeepSeek V3.2 offers comparable performance to leading proprietary models at a fraction of the cost.

claim: On the Aider polyglot leaderboard (225 multi-language Exercism exercises) frontier models GPT-5 (~0.880) and Claude Opus 4.6 (82.1%) lead, with open models trailing more on Go/Rust/Java than on Python-heavy SWE-bench.
quote: Aider's polyglot benchmark tests LLMs on 225 challenging Exercism coding exercises across C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, and Rust ... Claude Opus 4.6 leads Aider Polyglot (82.1%)
